text: {"components": [{"type": "claim", "quote": "In Switzerland, for vacuum cleaners the same efficiency requirements apply as those in effect in the EU.", "gist": "Switzerland applies the same EU efficiency requirements to vacuum cleaners."}, {"type": "number", "quote": "900 watts", "gist": "Maximum permissible power of vacuum cleaners"}, {"type": "number", "quote": "43 kilowatt hours (kWh)", "gist": "Maximum annual electricity consumption for vacuum cleaners with average use"}, {"type": "claim", "quote": "The provisional energy label for vacuum cleaners is no longer valid.", "gist": "The temporary energy label for vacuum cleaners is invalid."}, {"type": "entity", "quote": "The General Court of the European Union", "gist": "EU court that annulled a regulation"}, {"type": "date", "quote": "18.1.2019", "gist": "Date when the EU court annulled the regulation"}, {"type": "entity", "quote": "Delegated Regulation (EU) 665/2013 on the energy labelling on vacuum cleaners", "gist": "EU regulation on vacuum cleaner energy labelling that was annulled"}, {"type": "claim", "quote": "The provisions of the Swiss Energy Efficiency Regulation (EnEV), Annex 1.8, Section 4 are no longer legally binding.", "gist": "Swiss EnEV Annex 1.8 Section 4 provisions are no longer legally binding."}]}
